First-name variants: nicknames, spellings, cognates and compounds.

Source: R/data.R
first_name_pairs.Rd

Pairs of first names that are two forms of one given name, observed as the same person (one EMP_ID) across their own organization's Form 990 Part VII filings, 2010-2024 (15.0 million people). Built in synthid (dev/name-variants/; see the synthid vignette "First-name variants - how the table was built") and copied here by data-raw/first_name_pairs.R, with some columns dropped and a formal column added. Used by nickname_lookup().

Usage

first_name_pairs

Format

A data.table::data.table with 24,967 rows and 13 variables, keyed on name_short:

name_short, name_long

the pair, shorter form first

type

nickname, spelling, cognate, compound (lexicon), or sound_alike, misspelling (not lexicon)

lexicon

TRUE for the reviewed pairs

n_emp_ids

number of people carrying the pair

freq_short, freq_long

national Part VII rows with each first name

f_short, f_long

share of those rows recorded female

cofiling_rate

how often the two forms appear as separate people with one surname on one return, per person carrying the pair; high values are weaker evidence (JOHN/JOHNNY: father and son)

flags

"", "gender", "cofiling" or "cofiling gender"

chain_id

variant chain: connected component of the lexicon pairs

formal

nickname pairs only: "short" or "long", the side that is the formal name; NA for other types

Source

synthid dev/name-variants/first-name-variants.csv, commit 07c320f (2026-11-23).

Details

The 1,002 rows with lexicon = TRUE are the pairs seen in 25+ people, reviewed by hand. The other 23,965 rows are sound-alike and misspelling pairs from rarer pairs, not reviewed.
